newsitem.title: POLAND: NEW POLISH MINISTER FAVOURS LICENCING SUPERMARKETS.
newsitem.headline: NEW POLISH MINISTER FAVOURS LICENCING SUPERMARKETS.

text.p: Poland's Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said on Thursday he will not abandon his predecessor's plan to give local governments power to regulate setting up and operation of supermarkets.
"The go ahead for a supermarket would be given by a local self-government after consultations with a local chamber of commerce," Kaczmarek told a news briefing.

Plans to create a bill ending freedom to set up supermarkets were devised by Industry Minister Klemens Scierski, whose ministry was replaced by the economy portfolio this year under a major government reform.
Poland's small retailers are pressing the government to curb rapid expansion of supermarkets, which they say pushes them out of business.
The issue has become one of themes of campaign to this year's parliamentary elections, with some parties advocating stricter curbs on the growth of supermarkets.

Kaczmarek said he would abandon works on Scierski's programme called "Handel 2000," which provided for creating a fund or agency to give financial and other help for smaller retailers to cooperate in cutting costs and gaining credits.
"The programme was a collection of slogans which lack means of implementing them," he said.
